title: Attention's Advertising Strategy: The Category Winner That Barely Advertises
summary: Attention is Ramp's most-purchased AI GTM vendor at 34%, with 23 Meta ads, one headline on 26 of 27, 52 LinkedIn ads and 87 Google creatives. How it runs them.
body_markdown:
Ramp's October 2026 AI category data has Attention as the most-purchased vendor in AI-First GTM. 34% of the category's buyers.


Then you look at its ads. 23 live on Meta. One headline on 26 of 27. A Google account that is mostly one sentence. A LinkedIn account where most of the work is done by people who do not work in marketing.


A category winner whose growth is not coming from paid. Or at least, not from paid that anyone is tuning.


One of the live Meta creatives. Same headline as 25 others: "AI for sales teams". 13 October 2026.


## Attention ads: key findings


- **26 of 27** Meta ads use one headline: "AI for sales teams"
- **5** LinkedIn ads are promoted posts by people who don't work at Attention: customers and operators vouching in the first person
- **4** Google ad groups named after a competitor or a switch: Drift, Relevance AI, Jiminny, MCP
- **1** Google ad caught with its template showing: "<dynamically generated based on landing page content>"
- **404** on /pricing. Every path ends at a booking form, and the site identifies visitors who never fill it
- **0** affiliate, referral or creator programs. Agencies get "referral fees", amount unpublished
- **87** Google search creatives, **24** repeating "Iterating before ChatGPT", **28** still served in October 2026
- **0** UTM parameters on any Meta destination


## How Attention's funnel is wired


Attention's ads are thin on purpose. One Meta headline, one Google sentence. The work happens after the click, and in whose name the ad runs.


### Customers post the ads


11 LinkedIn ads are promoted posts by people rather than the company page. 5 of those people don't work at Attention.


Poster What the ad says


An AE at Engine "My Q2 is on pace to be 14x what I booked in Q3 last year. Not 14%. 14x."


Partnerships lead at DualEntry Every Monday and Wednesday, each AE gets a ranked list of co-sell plays in Slack before coffee


Growth lead at Netic A teardown of the sales stack Lovable scaled with


An operations executive "Quick shout out to the team at Attention. It's my new obsession."


An HR lead A shout-out after Attention sent him its latest Deal View update


Attention pays to put buyers' own posts in front of other buyers. The testimonial arrives with the customer's face, title and network attached, not as a quote on a landing page.


### Google ad groups are named after the tool you're leaving


The display URLs on Attention's search ads spell out the ad groups: /drift/alternative, /relevance-ai/alternative, /switch-to/attention-ai ("Attention Over Jiminny", "Time to Switch Platforms") and /mcp/attention-ai ("15 MCP Tool Groups. Not 3").


Those are display paths, not pages. Type any of them and you get a 404. They tell you how the account is cut: alternatives, switchers, MCP buyers, note-taker searches, sales teams.


One variation reads, word for word, "<dynamically generated based on landing page content>". That's a dynamic search ad with its template showing: Google writing the headline from the page.


### The website is the SDR


There's no pricing page. /pricing is a 404, and every route ends at a booking form. The homepage also loads RB2B, which identifies individual visitors, and Default.com, which routes and books inbound leads, on top of HubSpot.


So a paid click that never fills the form can still be named and routed to a rep. That's why the ads can be this thin. On Meta, 26 of 27 carry one headline, and the EU reach breakdowns count between 1 and 6 people per ad. Meta, in practice, is a US-only reminder.


## Who Attention pays to sell it


No affiliate program, no referral page (/affiliates and /referral are both 404s), no creator program. Attention's partner program courts RevOps and sales-enablement agencies with free certification, a directory listing, co-selling and "referral fees". The amount isn't published.


The free amplification comes from somewhere else: Ramp. Attention's CEO and its VP Growth both run LinkedIn ads built on Ramp's software adoption data, the same index that ranks Attention first among AI-First GTM vendors.


## Meta: one headline, two refreshes


### The headline is the whole account


I counted 27 Meta ads for[Attention](https://www.sprites.ai/attention-ads) , 23 of them live. 26 carry the headline "AI for sales teams". The other one, from October 2024, says "AI For Sales, Stop Worrying About Notes".


That is not A/B testing. Testing varies the headline. Here the headline is a constant and only the picture and the first line of body move.


Launch date Ads Status on 13 October 2026


14 Oct 2024 1 Ended 12 May 2026 (575 days)


22 Apr 2025 3 Ended 11-12 May 2026 (about 385 days each)


29 May 2026 8 Live


23 Jun 2026 7 Live


2 Sep 2026 6 Live (carousels)


1 Oct 2026 2 Live


Median ended ad lived 385 days. Median live ad is 112 days old. Everything running today was launched after 29 May.


So it is not literally set and forget. It is set, forget for a year, then replace the lot in one go. All four old ads were switched off within two days of each other, and the first replacements went live on 29 May.


### The body moved. The headline did not


The oldest ad sold the CRM pain: "Focus on Sales, not filling up the CRM", cleaner forecasting data for sales leaders and RevOps. 24 of the 27 bodies now open with "Launch custom AI agents in seconds with access to all your sales touchpoints". Two April 2025 ads sit in between with "AI sales intelligence that simplifies coaching, improves forecasting".


Notes became CRM updates became agents. The positioning travelled across 18 months. The headline stayed where it was.


An April 2025 ad, ended 12 May 2026. The agent pitch was already there. Meta format Ads


Single image 20


Carousel (two cards) 6


Video 1


All 27 point at attention.com, 23 to the homepage and 3 to the "AI for sales teams" page and 1 to a customer-calls page. No UTM tags on any of them.


## LinkedIn: where the effort went


52 ads. 32 video, 11 single image, 5 document ads, 4 message ads. This is the channel Attention actually works.


### A vertical play for Medicare sales


"Meet the AI Built for Medicare Sales - Booth 214, Medicarians." One of 6 versions, 3 of them video.


This is the only ad in the account written for one buyer. HIPAA-compliant notetaker. Script adherence and compliance monitoring. AI coaching "can 3x your rep to manager ratio". A trade-show booth number, and a row of insurance-agency logos along the bottom.


Everywhere else, Attention talks to "sales teams". Here it talks to the people working a Medicare enrolment floor.


### The guides


Document ad What it promises


Deal-risk guide 9 pages: the 3 risks to catch on a first call, 3 questions that follow


Urgency talk tracks 10 tracks, 14 pages: scenario, exact words, why it works


AE ramp plan 10 pages; ramp now averages 4.8 months per the Bridge Group, top teams 30 to 60 days


GO-GO guide Goals, Outcomes, Gaps, Options: a question bank per stage


CRISP audit 5-part audit of an AI GTM stack, with leaders from Clay, Zapier, Abridge, Unify and Cargo AI


None of the five mentions a product feature. They are for the rep and the manager, not the buyer.


The rest of the company-page work is thin. 12 ads say "Learn what Attention can do for you". 10 say "AI For Sales, Stop Worrying About Notes". 4 push the Super Agent: "Turn every signal in your GTM stack into instant insights and automated actions".


### The people do the selling


A promoted personal post leading with Ramp's April 2026 category page: Attention at 30% adoption.


11 of the 52 LinkedIn ads are promoted posts by 9 named people. Two of them lead with Ramp's own category data. A third opens: "My Q2 is on pace to be 14x what I booked in Q3 last year. Not 14%. 14x." Another is a new hire writing that he "walked into Attention last month expecting the same punchline."


Proof in the first person is the one thing a company cannot say in its own headline.


## Google: one sentence, still running


I expected this channel to be dead. It is not. 87 search creatives, 85 text and 2 image, all in the US. 28 were served as recently as October 2026.


What they say is nearly one line. 24 of the 87 carry "The first sales platform to use generative AI on the market. Iterating before ChatGPT."


Last served 13 October 2026. Google signal Creatives


"Iterating before ChatGPT" line 24


"Sales teams are switching to Attention" 7


Switch-to display path 7


"40% Win Rate Improvement" sitelink 4


Destination is the homepage 48


Where first-shown dates are recorded, they run from 27 November 2024 to 28 March 2025. Eight creatives. The other 79 carry no start date, so the account is older than anyone can date it from outside.


The switch-to ads show with.attention.com, a separate host for paid traffic that now simply redirects to the homepage. Ads showing it were still serving on 13 October. That is the Google account doing one job: catching someone who is already looking, and sending them to the same booking form as everyone else.


## What actually makes this work


Nothing here looks like a growth engine. One headline. A year between refreshes. Homepage destinations with no tracking tags.


It works because the buying decision is not made in the ad. By the time a sales leader sees "AI for sales teams" on Meta they have already heard of Attention from a peer, a rep's post or Ramp's own ranking. The ad confirms the name. Google catches the person comparing tools. LinkedIn hands the rep a guide.


If I were copying anything, I would copy the people posts. 11 ads, 9 names, no brand voice. Those are the ones Attention cannot write for itself.
